_about: The story of each version: its theme, what it feels like day to day, what it contemplates and why. Written from docs/research/plan-doc (01-the-plan, 02-why-each-stay-is-this-long, 03-what-were-missing) and the region guides. Stay notes say why a base gets that many nights in that version.

plan.theme: Snow country, crab season and a ryokan New Year
plan.tagline: Six bases, two or more nights everywhere, light afternoons.
plan.feel: An easy start in Tokyo while the jet lag wears off and the four first-timers get the classic days. Then the Hokuriku shinkansen to Kanazawa for the slow middle of the trip: a whole house with a kitchen and a washing machine, crab at its peak, the snow-roped pines of Kenroku-en, museums done by the 27th before they close. A bus over the mountains through Shirakawa-go's thatched farmhouses to Takayama's old town, then a 45-minute train down the valley to Gero to sit out the busiest travel days of the year in a ryokan: footbaths, kaiseki on New Year's Eve, the temple bell at midnight, a New Year breakfast. New Year's Day is the quiet day to travel, so that is when we go to Kyoto. Temples and the New Year rituals there, Nara's deer on the Monday when museums close, then the shinkansen and a bus to Lake Kawaguchi, where Fuji stands straight across the water from the room and the shore, with two dawns to catch it clear, and two last Tokyo days for the museums that were shut in December.
activities: Tokyo: Tsukiji and the Hama-rikyu garden, Meiji Jingu and the Nezu Museum, Asakusa, a free Fuji viewpoint, the illuminations
Kanazawa: Kenroku-en with the yukitsuri snow ropes, the castle park, the 21st Century Museum, Higashi Chaya and a gold-leaf workshop, the samurai house, Omicho market and kobako crab
Shirakawa-go: the thatched village in snow, on the bus between Kanazawa and Takayama
Takayama: the Jinya before it closes, the morning market, the sake breweries, Hida beef, Hida Folk Village
Gero: footbaths, three public baths with a ¥1,300 pass, the Gassho Village, kaiseki and the New Year's Eve bell
Kyoto and Nara: Higashiyama and Kiyomizu-dera, Arashiyama, Fushimi Inari at dawn for whoever wants an early start, the National Museum on 2–3 Jan, Nara on 4 Jan
Kawaguchiko: Fuji straight across the lake from Oishi Park, the Panoramic Ropeway and the lake boat, hoto noodles, Chureito Pagoda at dawn for whoever wants the climb
Tokyo again: the Musée d'Orsay show, the National Museum open late on Fri 8 Jan, last shopping and last meals
plan.why: It is the only version that works for everyone. Every stay is two nights or more, no long move falls on a peak travel day, New Year's Eve has dinner included, and afternoons are kept light. Days can split: João and Carolina can do two big things a day while she and the parents do one.
plan.suits: Her at 29–32 weeks (beds, few moves, private baths), the parents on a first visit, and the first-timers (João, Carolina and Tatiana) who want the classic sights without exhaustion.
plan.trade: Gives up Okuhida's snow baths and Hiroshima, both a night more than the calendar allows. And Hakone's five museums and ryokan baths: the lake has less to do indoors on a cloudy day, and it is an hour further from Kyoto.

stay_notes.tokyo: Arrival plus three full days. Jet lag and four first-timers need an easy start; Mon 21 Dec is a museum closing day, so it becomes the market-and-gardens day. One night less loses a whole side of the city.
stay_notes.kanazawa: Above the usual two or three days, deliberately: it is the slow stretch before New Year, it has the museums we care about, and everything must be done by Sun 27 Dec because museums close on Mon 28. A rental with a washing machine makes it the mid-trip reset.
stay_notes.takayama: The town fills one day and the Jinya closes on 29 Dec, so arrive about 13:30 on the 28th and see it that afternoon. One night more would buy the Okuhida ropeway and snow baths.
stay_notes.gero: Fixed by the calendar. Check in on 30 Dec, New Year's Eve at the ryokan, leave after the New Year breakfast on 1 Jan. One night would mean moving on 31 Dec, a peak travel day.
stay_notes.kyoto: Three big days plus Nara. Arrival on 1 Jan is late afternoon and counts as no day. Museums go on 2–3 Jan, Nara on Mon 4 Jan when Kyoto's museums close. One night less drops Nara or Arashiyama.
stay_notes.kawaguchiko: One full day for the ropeway and the lake, and two dawns for a clear Fuji. Arrival from Kyoto is mid-afternoon, so day one is the shore and the hotel. One night would give a single chance at Fuji after the longest move of the trip.
stay_notes.tokyo:2: The museums that were closed in December, shopping, and a buffer before the flight. One night is possible but leaves no slack if a train or the weather slips.

tokyo.longer: A fifth night buys Kamakura or Nikko as a day trip. The city can fill any number of days.
tokyo.shorter: Three nights means two full days: one classic day is lost for the four first-timers, and the jet lag lands on a travel day.
tokyo.note: No idle risk. Tokyo fills every day, indoors or out.

kanazawa.longer: A fifth night (28 Dec) is a museum-closed Monday: the market and the castle park, or a Kaga Onsen half day. Mostly a rest.
kanazawa.shorter: Three nights squeezes Kenroku-en, the museums and the geisha district into two days and loses the slow day before New Year.
kanazawa.note: Day four (Sun 27 Dec) is light by design: the market, a workshop, laundry. Fine as a rest, dull if you want to be out all day.

takayama.longer: A third night buys Okuhida: the ropeway and the snow baths, a long cold day. Otherwise it is a second walk through the same old town.
takayama.shorter: One night would mean seeing the Jinya and the old town in one afternoon, then leaving; just possible, but rushed.
takayama.note: Day two (Tue 29 Dec) has the Jinya, Kyoya and two museums shut. The folk village and the breweries are open; it is a half day of things.

gero.longer: A third night is a day at the inn. Gero is a spa town, not a sight: footbaths, three public baths, a small folk village. Pleasant, not beautiful.
gero.shorter: One night means moving on 31 Dec, the busiest travel day of the year, and no quiet day before the New Year dinner.
gero.note: Be honest about this one: the second day in Gero is for the bath, a nap and the kaiseki. If idle days bother you, this is the stop to question. The alternative is New Year in Takayama or Kyoto.

kyoto.longer: A fifth night buys an easy day for Ohara or Kibune, or a second temple morning for the early risers.
kyoto.shorter: Three nights loses Nara or Arashiyama, because 1 Jan is an arrival afternoon and most places are shut until the 2nd.
kyoto.note: 1 Jan is a quiet arrival day with restaurants closed: the house, a convenience store, a walk. Expected, and the only such day here.

kawaguchiko.longer: A third night is a third chance at a clear Fuji and an easy day: Oshino Hakkai's spring ponds or Lake Yamanaka, each about 30 minutes by bus. Otherwise there is little more to see.
kawaguchiko.shorter: One night gives one dawn and no ropeway day, after the longest move of the trip; the lake becomes a stopover.
kawaguchiko.note: Clear days are full. On a cloudy day there is less to do than in Hakone: the kimono museum, the music forest, the footbaths, a long hoto lunch. That is the cost of the better view.

tokyo:2.longer: A third night at the end buys a Kamakura day or a proper last shopping day, and more slack before a Saturday flight.
tokyo:2.shorter: One night is enough for the flight, not for the museums that were shut in December.

gentle.tagline: One outing a day, then rest. The fewest check-ins of any version.
gentle.feel: The same opening in Tokyo, then four long stays and only four packing days. Kanazawa and Kyoto each get an extra night, so every day there holds one thing in the morning and nothing after lunch. Takayama becomes a four-night mountain base with New Year's Eve at a ryokan in the old town, and Okuhida or Shirakawa-go as unhurried day trips. Fuji is seen from the shinkansen or a Tokyo tower, or on an optional day trip from the last three Tokyo nights.
activities: Tokyo: the three classic days, spread over four nights
Kanazawa: Kenroku-en, the 21st Century Museum, the chaya districts, a crab lunch, and a free day
Takayama: the old town and market, Hida Folk Village, a slow Shirakawa-go day, an optional Okuhida snow day, New Year's Eve at a Takayama ryokan
Kyoto: Higashiyama, Arashiyama, Nara, and an easy day for Kibune or Ohara
Tokyo: museums, shopping, and a Fuji day trip if anyone wants one: Kawaguchiko (2 h each way) or Hakone (80 minutes)
gentle.why: Built around her and the parents: beds, few moves, private baths, and no day that needs stamina. The easiest pace for a 29–32 week pregnancy.
gentle.suits: Her, the parents, and anyone who would rather see less and never be tired.
gentle.trade: Gives up the lake, the two Fuji dawns, and the onsen-town New Year's Eve. The first-timers see fewer places and João and Carolina may find it slow.

stay_notes.takayama: Four nights works at Gentle because the days stay half-empty: the old town, the folk village, Shirakawa-go and Okuhida as day trips, and New Year's Eve at a ryokan with dinner.
stay_notes.kyoto: Five nights gives a gentle day for Kibune or Ohara on top of the three big days and Nara.
stay_notes.tokyo:2: Three nights at the end leave room for a Fuji day trip (Hakone is about 80 minutes each way, Kawaguchiko two hours) or a rest day before the flight.

kanazawa.longer: There is nothing more to add; four nights already covers it with a rest day.
kanazawa.shorter: Three nights loses the rest day.
kanazawa.note: One free day is built in. Fine at a gentle pace.

takayama.longer: Nothing to add. Four nights is already generous for a one-day town.
takayama.shorter: Two nights loses the Shirakawa-go and Okuhida day trips and New Year in the old town.
takayama.note: Four nights in Takayama means two of the four days are day trips (Shirakawa-go, Okuhida) and 29–31 Dec have the museums shut. Without the day trips this is too long.

kyoto.longer: A sixth night is too many with the city half shut until 3 Jan.
kyoto.shorter: Four nights, as in the main route, loses the easy Ohara or Kibune day.
kyoto.note: 1 Jan is quiet by nature; the fifth day is a gentle one.

tokyo:2.shorter: Two nights loses the Fuji day trip and the rest day before the flight.
tokyo:2.note: Three nights at the end is easy to fill: museums, Kamakura, shopping.

full.theme: Everything, including the snow baths and Hiroshima
full.tagline: Eight bases, eight moves, two big things a day.
full.feel: A classic sightseeing trip. Tokyo and Kanazawa are trimmed to three nights, Okuhida's open-air baths in deep snow and the Shinhotaka ropeway go in between Takayama and Gero, and two Hiroshima nights with Miyajima follow Kyoto. The trade is time on trains: about 18 hours between bases, moves on 30 Dec and 4 Jan, one four-hour leg from Hiroshima to Hakone, and a single night in Tokyo at the end.
activities: Tokyo and Kanazawa in three nights each, two big things a day
Okuhida: rotenburo in the snow, the Shinhotaka ropeway to 2,156 m
Gero: the ryokan New Year's Eve
Kyoto in three nights, then Hiroshima's Peace Park and Miyajima's floating torii
Hakone's loop and Fuji, then one last Tokyo night
full.why: For the two who have been to Tokyo and Kyoto before, this is the version with five new places. It keeps Hakone rather than the lake because from Hiroshima the lake is about an hour further. It fits João and Carolina's wish to see a lot.
full.suits: João and Carolina. Pedro and Fernanda, for the new places.
full.trade: No rest days. Travel on the peak days 30 Dec and 4 Jan. A one-night stop at the end. Too tiring for her and probably for the parents.

stay_notes.okuhida: Two nights for the ropeway and the snow baths. New Year's Eve then falls in Gero after a 2-hour move on 30 Dec, a peak day.
stay_notes.hiroshima: Two nights: the Peace Park and museum on one day, Miyajima on the other. Getting there is a move on 4 Jan, a peak day; then about four and a half hours to Hakone on 6 Jan.
stay_notes.tokyo:2: One night. Enough for the flight, not for the museums.

tokyo.longer: Four nights gives the first-timers the third classic day.
tokyo.shorter: Two nights is too little for a first visit.
tokyo.note: Two big things a day; no idle risk, some tired legs.

kanazawa.longer: Four nights adds the rest day the main route has.
kanazawa.shorter: Two nights loses the museums or the geisha district.
kanazawa.note: Three nights is tight, not idle.

okuhida.longer: A third night is a second bath day in a hamlet with nothing else.
okuhida.shorter: A day trip from Takayama covers the ropeway and one bath without the move.
okuhida.note: Day two is the baths and the view. Beautiful, but there is nothing else to do; fine if a snow bath is the point.

hiroshima.longer: A third night buys Iwakuni or a second Miyajima evening.
hiroshima.shorter: One night means the Peace Park and Miyajima on the same day, which is a long day.

tokyo:2.longer: A second night buys the December museums back.

snow-monkeys.theme: The plan, with snow monkeys first
snow-monkeys.tagline: Two Nagano nights on the way to Kanazawa; the rest unchanged.
snow-monkeys.feel: Tokyo is cut to three nights and Kanazawa to three, which buys two nights in Yudanaka: wild macaques in a steaming pool in a snowy gorge, and Shibu Onsen's lantern-lit street of nine old public baths. It sits on the shinkansen line, so the detour is about 80 minutes to Nagano and a 40-minute bus. From there the trip runs exactly as the plan: Kanazawa, Takayama, Gero for New Year's Eve, Kyoto, Kawaguchiko, Tokyo.
activities: Yudanaka: the snow monkey park (a 30–40 minute forest walk on packed snow), Shibu Onsen's bath-hopping street, a ryokan dinner; Obuse's Hokusai museum on the way
Everything in the plan, with one day less in Tokyo and Kanazawa
snow-monkeys.why: Yudanaka is the one new place that adds something genuinely different at an easy pace, and it replaces nights rather than adding them.
snow-monkeys.suits: Anyone whose must-do is the snow monkeys. Works for the parents; she can wait at the ryokan if the path is icy.
snow-monkeys.trade: A Tokyo day and Kanazawa's fourth night, which was the rest day before New Year. Snow can be thin in late December.

stay_notes.yudanaka: Two nights: one for the monkeys, one for the onsen street. The forest path can be icy; cleats and a slow pace, or she stays at the ryokan.
stay_notes.tokyo: Three nights means two full days. The parents lose one classic day; it can be made up on 7–8 Jan.
stay_notes.kanazawa: Three nights means the museums day becomes a long one, or the Museum of Art drops out.

yudanaka.longer: A third night buys Nozawa or Zenko-ji; otherwise it is a second bath day.
yudanaka.shorter: One night makes the monkeys a rushed morning after a late arrival.
yudanaka.note: Day two is the bath street and a slow lunch. Lovely in snow, quiet without it.

tokyo.longer: Four nights gives back the classic day the first-timers lose here.
tokyo.shorter: Two nights is too little for a first visit.

kanazawa.longer: Four nights gives back the rest day.
kanazawa.shorter: Two nights loses the museums or the geisha district.
kanazawa.note: Three nights is full, not idle.

art-not-fuji.theme: Art islands and gardens instead of Fuji
art-not-fuji.tagline: Okayama replaces Kawaguchiko: Naoshima, Kurashiki, Korakuen and Himeji.
art-not-fuji.feel: Identical to the plan until Kyoto. Then an hour west to Okayama for two nights: Himeji Castle on the way (Tue 5 Jan, she stays in the grounds), Korakuen's New Year garden, Kurashiki's canal and the Ohara Museum, and a day on Naoshima for the Chichu Art Museum and Benesse House on Wed 6 Jan, when it is open. The ride back to Tokyo is three hours twenty on the Sanyo and Tokaido shinkansen.
activities: Himeji Castle, Japan's finest original keep
Korakuen, one of the three great gardens; Kurashiki's canal quarter and the Ohara Museum
Naoshima: Chichu Art Museum (timed tickets), Benesse House, the Yellow Pumpkin
Everything in the plan up to Kyoto
art-not-fuji.why: For a family that values museums and architecture, Naoshima is the strongest single addition. Flat towns suit her and the parents.
art-not-fuji.suits: The museum lovers. Those who have already seen Fuji.
art-not-fuji.trade: The lake and the two Fuji dawns. Island walking in a cold sea wind; Chichu is closed Mondays.

stay_notes.okayama: Two nights: Himeji on the way in and Korakuen or Kurashiki on 5 Jan, Naoshima on Wed 6 Jan (Chichu closed Mondays; Teshima closed Tue–Thu in winter). Then about 3 h 20 to Tokyo.

okayama.longer: A third night adds Kurashiki properly or Teshima if it is open.
okayama.shorter: One night loses Naoshima, which is the point.
okayama.note: Himeji on the way in, Naoshima on the full day. No idle risk if the ferry runs.

kinosaki.theme: Crab and seven baths instead of Fuji
kinosaki.tagline: Kinosaki Onsen replaces Kawaguchiko, in snow-crab season.
kinosaki.feel: Identical to the plan until Kyoto. Then 2 h 50 north-west to Kinosaki: a willow-lined canal town where everyone walks between seven public baths in yukata and geta, with a crab kaiseki at the ryokan. The town is flat, which suits the parents; she keeps to the ryokan's private bath because the public ones run hot. The catch is the way home: five to six hours back to Tokyo on 7 Jan.
activities: The seven public baths of Kinosaki, by yukata and geta
Snow-crab kaiseki at the ryokan, in season
The ropeway and Onsen-ji temple
Everything in the plan up to Kyoto
kinosaki.why: A classic onsen town at its best moment, for a family that liked the idea of the ryokan night and wants a second one.
kinosaki.suits: Onsen and crab lovers. Flat streets suit the parents.
kinosaki.trade: The lake and Fuji, a 5–6 hour journey back to Tokyo, and it repeats Kanazawa's crab and Gero's onsen.

stay_notes.kinosaki: Two nights, the usual minimum for its New Year and crab-season plans. Book a ryokan with a private bath for her; the Nishimuraya houses have Western beds and a lift.

kinosaki.longer: A third night is a third evening of baths and crab in the same small town.
kinosaki.shorter: One night is a long way to go for one dinner.
kinosaki.note: Day two is the baths, the ropeway and the temple. Pleasant and slow; like Gero, the town is the inn.

fuji-lake.tagline: Five museums and a ryokan with a private bath in every room; the rest of the route unchanged.
fuji-lake.feel: Identical to the route until Kyoto. Then the Hikari to Odawara, seats on the Fuji side, and the mountain railway up into Hakone: about three and a quarter hours, an hour less than the lake. Steam, pines, a ryokan with an open-air bath in every room for the three couples, and kaiseki at the inn. One full day for the loop by railway, ropeway and boat, the Open-Air Museum or the Pola for a cloudy morning, and two dawns to catch Fuji over the lake. Then 80 minutes on the Romancecar to Shinjuku for the last Tokyo days. Fuji shows fully on about six January mornings in ten; from Hakone it rises behind the ridges, so a clear morning matters more.
activities: The Hakone loop: mountain railway, cable car, the ropeway over Owakudani's steam, the boat across Lake Ashi
The Open-Air Museum's sculpture park and Picasso pavilion, or the Pola Museum's Impressionists if it rains
Hatsuhana soba in Yumoto on arrival (closed Wednesdays)
A ryokan with an open-air bath in every room and kaiseki at dinner
Fuji over the lake from the Narukawa museum lounge or Onshi-Hakone Park (about 200 steps to the lookout)
Everything in the route up to Kyoto, and the two Tokyo days after
fuji-lake.why: Hakone is the better bet if the weather turns: five museums fill a cloudy day, the ryokan with private baths are the real thing, and it is an hour closer to Kyoto and 80 minutes from Shinjuku. It is new for everyone except Pedro and Fernanda.
fuji-lake.suits: Anyone who wants a proper ryokan night and museums in reserve. The ropeway crosses volcanic gas, so she checks with her doctor; everything else is seated, and the private bath makes the onsen easy.
fuji-lake.trade: Fuji straight across the water: in Hakone the mountain shows over the ridges and cloud on the ridge line can hide it. And it repeats a place Pedro and Fernanda have already done.

stay_notes.hakone: Two nights, like the lake: one full day for the loop and a museum, and two dawns for a clear Fuji. The Ekiden relay closes the roads on 2–3 Jan; 5–7 Jan is clear. Arrival from Kyoto is early afternoon, in time for Hatsuhana soba on Tue 5 Jan.

hakone.longer: A third night is a second chance at Fuji and a second museum day. Hakone has five museums, so a cloudy extra day is not wasted.
hakone.shorter: One night gives one morning for Fuji and no time for the loop; the ryokan becomes a stopover.
hakone.note: Two full mornings and one full day. On a cloudy day the museums fill it.

golden-route-winter.theme: Tokyo to the floating torii, the classic way
golden-route-winter.tagline: Tokyo 3, Hakone 2, Kyoto 3, Hiroshima 2, Miyajima 2, Osaka 5 and Tokyo 3: the first-timer's Japan, with New Year's Eve at a ryokan beside the floating torii.
golden-route-winter.feel: It opens in Tokyo in lights week: markets, Asakusa and an izakaya night while the Christmas illuminations are still up. Then Christmas Eve at a Hakone ryokan with a private bath, and Fuji at dawn before the train west. Kyoto gets three busy days while every temple, museum and market is open. Hiroshima comes next, with the Peace Park and okonomiyaki on the last ordinary days of the year. On 30 Dec a short ferry takes you to Miyajima for New Year's Eve: the fire festival on the shore, a ryokan dinner and the shrine opening at midnight. New Year's Day is a quiet train to Osaka, which is the right city for the shutdown: the chains on Dotonbori stay open, the castle reopens on 2 Jan, and Nara and Himeji are short hops. Three easy days in Tokyo close it.
activities: Tokyo (start): Tsukiji outer market and Hama-rikyu, Asakusa and Senso-ji, Meiji Jingu and Harajuku, the Christmas lights
Hakone: Open-Air Museum, the ropeway and Lake Ashi loop, Fuji at dawn, a ryokan with a private bath on Christmas Eve
Kyoto: Kiyomizu-dera and Higashiyama, Kyoto National Museum, Arashiyama and Tenryu-ji, Kinkaku-ji, Fushimi Inari at dawn for the the early risers
Hiroshima: Peace Memorial Park and Museum (open 28–29 Dec), okonomiyaki, Iwakuni's Kintai bridge for the keen
Miyajima: Itsukushima Shrine at high and low tide, the Chinka-sai fire festival on 31 Dec, grilled oysters (cooked), Momijidani park
Osaka: Dotonbori lights, Osaka Castle from 2 Jan, Kaiyukan aquarium, Bunraku New Year programme, Kuromon market from 5 Jan
Day trips from Osaka: Nara (Todai-ji, the deer, Kasuga Taisha) on 4 Jan and Himeji Castle on 5 Jan
Tokyo (end): Tokyo National Museum and Ueno once reopened, a single act at Kabuki-za, last shopping and a farewell dinner
golden-route-winter.why: This is the route most first-timers take, and for good reason: it strings Japan's best-known sights along one shinkansen line with no buses. It is adapted to the New Year by doing Kyoto and Hiroshima before the shutdown, spending New Year's Eve at a ryokan on Miyajima, and sitting out 1–5 Jan in Osaka, the big city that copes best with closures.
golden-route-winter.suits: João, Carolina and Tatiana, who want the famous sights on a first visit; Carlos and Nadir, for Hiroshima and Miyajima's history. Pedro and Fernanda get Hiroshima, Miyajima and Himeji as new places, and know Kyoto and Osaka well enough to set an easy pace there.
golden-route-winter.trade: No snow at all: no Kanazawa, Shirakawa-go or Takayama, and no snow-country onsen. Kyoto gets three nights instead of four, and seven stays mean more packing than the main route. Pedro and Fernanda have already seen Tokyo, Hakone, Kyoto and Osaka.
golden-route-winter.nye: On Miyajima, at a ryokan with New Year's Eve dinner and toshikoshi soba. The Chinka-sai fire festival runs on Mikasa-hama beach from 18:00 to 18:30 (watch from the back of the crowd), and Itsukushima Shrine opens at midnight for the first visit of the year. Fernanda can see the shrine calmly on 30 or 31 Dec in daylight instead of joining the midnight queue; the the early risers can ring in the year at Daisho-in, where the first 108 people in line from about 21:00 strike the bell.

stay_notes.tokyo: Arrival plus two full days while the Christmas lights are up. Short, because Tokyo comes back at the end when the museums have reopened.
stay_notes.hakone: Christmas Eve and Christmas morning at a ryokan, one full day for the Hakone loop and two dawns to catch Fuji clear. December mornings are the clearest of the year.
stay_notes.kyoto: Three nights while everything is open: one afternoon and two full days for Higashiyama, the National Museum, Arashiyama and Kinkaku-ji. Kyoto is also a 30-minute day trip from Osaka in January.
stay_notes.hiroshima: Arrive by lunch on 28 Dec and see the Peace Museum that afternoon or the next morning, before it closes on 30–31 Dec. Two nights keep the last ordinary restaurant evenings for okonomiyaki.
stay_notes.miyajima: New Year's Eve on the island, reached by a 40-minute hop on 30 Dec, which avoids a long train on the peak days. Two nights give a calm day on the island before the crowds come over.
stay_notes.osaka: Five nights across the shutdown in the city that handles it best: chain restaurants and Dotonbori stay open, the castle reopens on 2 Jan, and Nara, Kyoto and Himeji are under an hour away. It also waits out the return peak of 2–4 Jan without a long move.
stay_notes.tokyo:2: Two full days and a calm last night near Haneda. The National Museum, Ueno and Kabuki-za are all running again by now.

tokyo.longer: A day trip to Kamakura or Nikko before Christmas
tokyo.shorter: Arriving and leaving within two days, with jet lag
tokyo.note: Full days; jet lag will set the pace on 21 Dec.

hakone.longer: A real rest day in the ryokan, and a third chance at a clear Fuji
hakone.shorter: One night means Fuji only if the single morning is clear
hakone.note: One full day and two short ones; the bath does the resting.

kyoto.longer: Fushimi Inari, Nijo Castle or Ohara for everyone, not just the the early risers
kyoto.shorter: Two nights would leave only the headline temples
kyoto.note: The busiest stretch of the trip; the 2–4 pm break matters here.

hiroshima.longer: A day for Iwakuni and the Kintai bridge, but 30 Dec is a peak travel day
hiroshima.shorter: One night would rush the Peace Museum
hiroshima.note: One afternoon and one full day, both well used.

miyajima.longer: Staying to 2 Jan means a 1 Jan crowd on the island and a move on a peak day
miyajima.shorter: One night would mean arriving on 31 Dec, a busy morning on the trains
miyajima.note: 31 Dec is deliberately slow: a walk, a bath, the festival, dinner.

osaka.longer: Another day trip (Kobe, Arima or Uji), but Tokyo would lose a day
osaka.shorter: Moving on 5 Jan loses Himeji or Kuromon's first full day back
osaka.note: 1 and 3 Jan are light days by design; the city is half shut until 4 Jan.

tokyo:2.longer: A Fuji or Kamakura day trip
tokyo:2.shorter: Two nights would leave one day for the museums and packing
tokyo:2.note: 8 Jan is free on purpose, with bags already sent to the airport.

days.2026-12-20: Land at Haneda, jumbo taxi to the hotel, Marunouchi lights and an easy dinner
days.2026-12-21: Monday museum closures, so Tsukiji outer market, Hama-rikyu garden and a Ginza food hall
days.2026-12-22: Asakusa and Senso-ji in the morning, Skytree at dusk; send the big bags to Kyoto

two-cities-deep.theme: Two homes, many day trips, two train journeys
two-cities-deep.tagline: Tokyo 6, Kyoto 10 and Tokyo 4: two bases, only two long trains, day trips instead of moves, and New Year in Kyoto's temples from a house of your own.
two-cities-deep.feel: Six nights in Tokyo with no packing: the markets, Asakusa and the lights, then day trips out and back to Nikko's shrines in the cedars, Kamakura's Great Buddha and the deep snow at Echigo-Yuzawa, 75 minutes away. On 26 Dec one train takes you to Kyoto and a whole townhouse with a kitchen, a washing machine and a living room for seven. From there the days go out like spokes: Osaka for the castle and Dotonbori before it closes, Higashiyama and Arashiyama while the temples are quiet, Nishiki market to stock up on 30 Dec. New Year's Eve is at home with osechi and soba, then the sacred fire at Yasaka and the great bell at Chion-in. Nara at dawn on 1 Jan, Uji and Himeji after. Four calm days back in Tokyo finish it.
activities: Tokyo (start): Tsukiji outer market and Hama-rikyu, Asakusa and Senso-ji, Meiji Jingu, the Christmas illuminations
Day trips from Tokyo: Nikko's Toshogu, Kamakura's Great Buddha with Yokohama in the evening, Echigo-Yuzawa's snow and sake hall
Kyoto: Kiyomizu-dera and Higashiyama, Arashiyama and Tenryu-ji, Kinkaku-ji, Kyoto National Museum on 2–3 Jan, Kitano's first-calligraphy festival on 2 Jan
Kyoto New Year: Nishiki market on 30 Dec, Okera-mairi fire at Yasaka and the Chion-in bell on 31 Dec, osechi at home
Day trips from Kyoto: Osaka (castle, Kuromon, Dotonbori) on 27 Dec, Nara at dawn on 1 Jan, Uji's Byodo-in and matcha street, Himeji on 4 Jan
Optional from Kyoto: Ohara's Sanzen-in in the hills, or a half day at Arima Onsen near Kobe (not 1 Jan)
Tokyo (end): Tokyo National Museum, the Imperial Palace East Gardens, a Kabuki-za single act, a Fuji or Hakone day
two-cities-deep.why: It has the easiest logistics of any option: three check-ins, two long trains, a washing machine at every base and a home for the shutdown. It suits a group of seven with a pregnancy, because nobody packs between 26 Dec and 5 Jan, and every day out can be cut short with a 30-minute train home.
two-cities-deep.suits: Fernanda first, and Carlos and Nadir, who get Japan without the logistics. João, Carolina and Tatiana still see Tokyo, Kyoto, Osaka, Nara, Nikko and Himeji. Pedro gets one booking per city and empty evenings.
two-cities-deep.trade: No ryokan night and no onsen town, unless Arima is added as a half day. Less of rural Japan: no Shirakawa-go, Takayama or Kanazawa, and snow only on the Echigo-Yuzawa day. Fuji is a long day trip from Tokyo, not a stay. Pedro and Fernanda have seen both cities before.
two-cities-deep.nye: At the Kyoto house. Collect a pre-ordered osechi box from a department store food hall on 31 Dec (they take orders until about 22 Dec and hand them over 11:00–16:00), cook toshikoshi soba at home, then walk to Yasaka Shrine at 18:00–20:00 to light a rope from the Okera fire before the crush. The fit four can go on to Chion-in, where the 70-ton bell is struck from about 22:40 (viewing only, standing in the cold). Restaurants close, so a house with a kitchen and a living room is the warm, unhurried answer.

stay_notes.tokyo: Arrival, three city days and three day trips (Nikko, Kamakura with Yokohama, Echigo-Yuzawa) without moving hotel. Six nights also covers the Christmas lights, which end on 25 Dec.
stay_notes.kyoto: Ten nights from before the shutdown to after the return peak, so the 29 Dec – 4 Jan window needs no move at all. Kyoto alone fills five or six days; the rest are day trips to Osaka, Nara, Uji and Himeji, and easy days at home.
stay_notes.tokyo:2: Three full days once Tokyo has reopened: the National Museum, the palace gardens and Kabuki, plus an optional Fuji day, and a calm last night near the airport.

deep-snow-country.theme: Three weeks in the Alps and the snowy side
deep-snow-country.tagline: Tokyo 3, Nagano 3, Takayama 3, Okuhida 3, Kanazawa 4 and Tokyo 4: snow monkeys, thatched villages, a ryokan New Year in deep snow and Kanazawa's gardens under their snow ropes.
deep-snow-country.feel: Three days of Tokyo lights, then the shinkansen climbs into the mountains. In Nagano you watch the dawn service at Zenko-ji, the fit five walk the forest path to the snow monkeys, and Christmas Day is a trip to Matsumoto's black castle with the Alps behind it. The Hida line follows a white gorge to Takayama: morning markets, sake breweries, a day among the thatched farmhouses of Shirakawa-go. On 29 Dec a short bus ride takes you up to Okuhida, where the snow is deepest and New Year's Eve is a long dinner at a ryokan, with a private bath and a ropeway up to 2,156 m the day before. On the quiet 1 Jan you come down to Kanazawa for its slow, free New Year days in Kenroku-en. You end with four easy days in Tokyo and one last snow day at Echigo-Yuzawa.
activities: Tokyo: Christmas illuminations, Tsukiji outer market and Hama-rikyu on the Monday museums close, Asakusa and Ueno
Nagano: Zenko-ji at dawn and its pitch-dark o-kaidan passage, the Jigokudani snow monkeys, a day trip to Matsumoto Castle and Nakamachi, Obuse for Hokusai and chestnut sweets
Takayama: Takayama Jinya before it closes on 29 Dec, morning markets, Sanmachi sake breweries, Hida beef, a day trip to Shirakawa-go by bus
Okuhida: a ryokan New Year's Eve with private baths in deep snow, the Shin-Hotaka double-decker ropeway, Hirayu Great Falls, a guided snowshoe walk for the fit
Kanazawa: Kenroku-en free on 1–3 Jan with its yukitsuri snow ropes, the 21st Century Museum from 2 Jan, Higashi Chaya and gold leaf, Omicho's crab when it reopens on 5 Jan
Tokyo: Tokyo National Museum and the January Kabuki, shopping, and a snow-play day trip to GALA Yuzawa (75 minutes away)
deep-snow-country.why: This is the route for a family that came to Japan for winter itself: it stays on the snowy side of the mountains for two weeks instead of dipping in and out. It suits the first-timers who want the postcard Japan of snow and thatch, and it gives Pedro and Fernanda a trip with no Kyoto or Hakone repeats at all.
deep-snow-country.suits: João and Carolina (snow, monkeys, snowshoes), Carlos and Nadir (castle, villages, long walks in the snow), Tatiana (the classic winter images); Pedro and Fernanda get an all-new trip, though Fernanda has the most ice to manage of any option.
deep-snow-country.trade: No Kyoto, Nara or Fuji at all, so the first-timers miss Japan's temple capital and the famous mountain. There is more ice underfoot for Fernanda than on the main route, and New Year's Eve is about an hour from the nearest hospital with obstetrics rather than in a city. Five moves, and the 1 Jan journey is close to four hours.
deep-snow-country.nye: At a ryokan in Okuhida (Hirayu or Shin-Hotaka), with New Year's Eve kaiseki and toshikoshi soba included, a private or in-room bath for Fernanda, and snow banked up outside the window. Breakfast on 1 Jan is the New Year osechi before the quiet-day journey to Kanazawa.

stay_notes.tokyo: Arrival plus two full days to get over the flight; the city comes back at the end, so this first visit can stay light.
stay_notes.nagano: Arrival afternoon at Zenko-ji, then one day for the snow monkeys and one for Matsumoto Castle, which is open until 28 Dec and closed 29–31 Dec. Nagano is a flat city with trains in every direction and a Red Cross hospital.
stay_notes.takayama: Three nights so the Jinya (closed from 29 Dec), the old town and a full Shirakawa-go day all fit before New Year, without rushing on icy streets.
stay_notes.okuhida: Fixed by the calendar: in by 29 Dec on a one-hour bus, out on the quiet 1 Jan. Three nights gives one ropeway day, one slow day and New Year's Eve itself.
stay_notes.kanazawa: 1–4 Jan are slow days everywhere; Kanazawa is a home-coming city, not a resort, so it stays calm. Kenroku-en is free, the 21st Century Museum reopens on 2 Jan and Omicho fully reopens on 5 Jan, the morning you leave.
stay_notes.tokyo:2: Four nights so the museums closed in December can be seen, a snow-play day at Echigo-Yuzawa fits, and the last night is close to the airport.

western-onsen-trail.theme: Three great hot-spring towns, with Kyoto between
western-onsen-trail.tagline: Tokyo 2, Hakone 2, Kyoto 4, Kinosaki 4, Arima 4 and Tokyo 4: ten nights in onsen ryokan, a yukata New Year in Kinosaki and Japan's oldest hot spring for the first days of 2027.
western-onsen-trail.feel: After two Tokyo days the trip slows straight away: a Romancecar to Hakone, an in-room bath, Fuji over the ridges and the Open-Air Museum. Christmas Eve is in Kyoto, with four days of temples, Gion lanes and Nara's deer before everything closes. On 28 Dec a direct train runs north to Kinosaki, the willow-lined canal town where everyone walks between baths in yukata and wooden sandals. It is liveliest at New Year: crab dinners, the ropeway, a half day in the castle town of Izushi, then New Year's Eve at the inn. On the quiet 1 Jan you move to Arima, in the hills behind Kobe, for the first-bath ceremony on 2 Jan, a Kobe day and Himeji Castle. Four Tokyo nights close the trip.
activities: Tokyo: Tsukiji outer market and Hama-rikyu on the Monday, Ginza food halls and the Christmas lights
Hakone: an in-room bath for each couple, the Hakone Open-Air Museum and its foot bath, Pola Museum, Fuji from Lake Ashi
Kyoto: Higashiyama and Kiyomizu-dera, Fushimi Inari's lower shrines early, Arashiyama, and a Nara day before the New Year crowds
Kinosaki: the canal-side public baths in yukata (others) and private baths at the inn (her), snow-crab kaiseki, the ropeway and Onsen-ji, a half day in Izushi for sara soba
Arima: the Irizome-shiki first-bath ceremony on 2 Jan, Gin-no-yu's cooler carbonated bath, the hill lanes, a Kobe day and Himeji Castle on 4 Jan
Tokyo: Tokyo National Museum, New Year Kabuki, last shopping
western-onsen-trail.why: This route is built around bathing well, which suits Fernanda better than any snow walk: three onsen towns where she can soak in private, gently and often, while the others try the famous public baths. Kyoto gives the first-timers their temples in between, and Kinosaki at New Year is one of Japan's happiest places to be.
western-onsen-trail.suits: Fernanda (private baths, flat Kinosaki, cooked crab), Carlos and Nadir (bath-hopping in yukata, Kyoto, Himeji), Tatiana and Carolina (the ryokan life); João gets Himeji and Kobe but little snow.
western-onsen-trail.trade: No Kanazawa, Takayama, Shirakawa-go or real snow: Kinosaki may be white, the rest probably not. Hakone and Kyoto are repeats for Pedro and Fernanda. Ten ryokan nights make it the dearest of these three, and the last move from Arima to Tokyo is about four hours.
western-onsen-trail.nye: At a Kinosaki ryokan on a two-night New Year plan: snow-crab dinner (cooked for her), toshikoshi soba, osechi on 1 Jan. The town is at its liveliest, with families in yukata walking the canal between the public baths late into the night; Fernanda uses the inn's private bath, which in Kinosaki is plain heated water she can set to her own temperature.

stay_notes.tokyo: Arrival plus one full day; Tokyo returns for four nights at the end, so the start is just a soft landing.
stay_notes.hakone: Two nights in a ryokan is the classic length: one full day for the museums and two dawns for a clear Fuji, before the holiday rush.
stay_notes.kyoto: Four nights while the temples are calm and before the 29 Dec closures: Higashiyama, Fushimi Inari, Arashiyama and a Nara day.
stay_notes.kinosaki: Fixed by the calendar: in on 28 Dec, before the peak days, and out on the quiet 1 Jan. The town is small, so the four days are baths, crab, the ropeway, Izushi and doing very little.
stay_notes.arima: In on 1 Jan, out on 5 Jan after the return rush. Arima itself is a day; the other days are the 2 Jan ceremony, Kobe and Himeji, each under an hour away.
stay_notes.tokyo:2: The museums closed in December, Kabuki from 2 Jan, and a calm last night close to the airport.

slow-kyoto-and-the-sea.theme: Three homes, two train rides, no rushing
slow-kyoto-and-the-sea.tagline: Tokyo 4, a Kyoto house for 12 and a seaside hotel in Kamakura for 4: the fewest moves of any option, with New Year lived like a Kyoto family.
slow-kyoto-and-the-sea.feel: Four unhurried days in Tokyo, then on Christmas Eve one train ride to Kyoto and a house with four bedrooms, a kitchen and two bathrooms near the Heian shrine. You stay twelve nights. Each day holds one easy thing: Higashiyama's lanes, Nara's deer, the trial ringing of Chion-in's great bell on 27 Dec, Uji's tea houses, a snow day above Lake Biwa for anyone who wants one. New Year's Eve is at home with soba, then a short walk to Yasaka Shrine for the sacred okera fire, while the fit ones queue to ring a temple bell at midnight. The New Year days are slow and local, with Kyoto University Hospital ten minutes away. On 5 Jan you move once more, to a hotel above the sea at Kamakura: the Great Buddha, the little Enoden train, and Fuji across the bay at sunset.
activities: Tokyo: Tsukiji outer market and Hama-rikyu, Meiji Jingu and Harajuku, Asakusa and Ueno, the Christmas lights
Kyoto: Higashiyama and Gion, Fushimi Inari's lower shrines, Arashiyama, the Kyoto National Museum from 2 Jan, Ohara's quiet Sanzen-in on New Year's Day
From the Kyoto house: Nara and Todai-ji, Uji's Byodo-in and tea, Omi-Hachiman's canals on Lake Biwa, Himeji Castle, and a Biwako Valley snow day for the fit
New Year in Kyoto: Chion-in's trial bell ringing on 27 Dec, the okera fire at Yasaka on 31 Dec, a bell to ring at Kodai-ji or Eikando for the fit ones
Kamakura: the Great Buddha, Hase-dera's lower garden, the Enoden along the coast, Enoshima, Fuji over Sagami Bay at sunset, and a Yokohama day
slow-kyoto-and-the-sea.why: This is the route built around Fernanda and the parents: only two moving days, a real home for the twelve middle nights, and every New Year night in a city with a university hospital. It still gives the first-timers Tokyo, Kyoto, Nara and Fuji, and it is the cheapest of these three by a distance.
slow-kyoto-and-the-sea.suits: Fernanda first of all (two moves, her own ground-floor room, the hospital close), Carlos and Nadir (Kyoto in depth, Kamakura's temples), Tatiana (a living room to share); João and Carolina can take the snow day and the long Fushimi climb.
slow-kyoto-and-the-sea.trade: No Kanazawa, Takayama, Shirakawa-go or onsen town, and no real snow. Tokyo and Kyoto are repeats for Pedro and Fernanda, and New Year's Eve is a home dinner rather than a ryokan. Twelve nights in one city means some days with very little planned.
slow-kyoto-and-the-sea.nye: At the Kyoto house, argued on purpose: it is Japan's great New Year city, the house has a kitchen and a table for seven, and Kyoto University Hospital is ten minutes away when clinics are closed. Order an osechi box from a department store by mid-December, have toshikoshi soba at home or early at a soba shop, then walk to Yasaka Shrine around 19:30 for the okera fire before the midnight crowds. The fit ones queue for a bell they can ring (Kodai-ji, Chishaku-in or Eikando) while Fernanda goes home to bed.

stay_notes.tokyo: Arrival plus three easy days; Tokyo is not repeated at the end, so the first-timers get their Tokyo here while the Christmas lights are on.
stay_notes.kyoto: Twelve nights so that nobody packs between Christmas and Epiphany: the house covers the calm days before 29 Dec, the closed days, and the reopening on 2–4 Jan, with a different day trip whenever the city feels small.
stay_notes.kamakura: In after the return rush, out to the airport in about an hour. Four nights gives the Great Buddha, Enoshima, a Yokohama or Tokyo day, and a free last day.

west-castles-inland-sea.theme: Western Japan by rail, Kyoto to Izumo
west-castles-inland-sea.tagline: Six bases over 20 nights (Tokyo 3, Kyoto 3, Hiroshima 2, Matsue 4, Kurashiki 4, Tokyo 4), following the shinkansen west and crossing the mountains to the Sea of Japan coast for New Year.
west-castles-inland-sea.feel: Three days in Tokyo to find your feet, then Kyoto in the last calm week before the holidays, when the museums and theatres are open and the Shimai-Tenjin flea market fills Kitano Tenmangu on Christmas Day. The bullet train carries you on to Hiroshima for the Peace Park and a slow, full day on Miyajima, then over the Chugoku mountains to Matsue, a castle town on a lake famous for its sunsets. New Year is spent there at a lakeside onsen hotel, with Izumo Taisha visited the day before the pilgrims arrive and the Adachi garden in its winter quiet. On New Year's Day a two-hour train drops you in Kurashiki's willow-lined canal quarter, with Okayama's great garden and Himeji Castle a short ride away. The last four days in Tokyo pick up everything that was closed in December.
activities: Tokyo: Tsukiji outer market and Hama-rikyu on the museum-closed Monday, Meiji Jingu and the Nezu Museum, Asakusa

Kyoto: Kiyomizu-dera and the Higashiyama lanes, the last flea market of the year at Kitano Tenmangu on 25 Dec, the Kaomise kabuki at Minamiza if it is still running, Arashiyama at dawn for the early risers
Hiroshima: the Peace Park and Museum, okonomiyaki, the Dreamination lights, a day on Miyajima with grilled oysters and the Mt Misen ropeway
Matsue: sunset over Lake Shinji, the Adachi Museum of Art and its garden, Izumo Taisha on 30 Dec, Matsue Castle and the heated kotatsu boats on the castle moat
Kurashiki and Okayama: the Bikan canal quarter and the Ohara Museum, Korakuen's New Year festival with its red-crowned cranes, Himeji Castle on 4 Jan
Tokyo again: Tokyo National Museum and the Ueno museums, a single act at Kabuki-za, the New Year firemen's parade on 6 Jan, a calm day in Kamakura
west-castles-inland-sea.why: This is the route for castles, gardens and old shrines, and for seeing a side of Japan that most first visits miss. It runs west with the shinkansen, so every move is short except the crossing to the San'in coast and the ride home. It suits Carlos and Nadir, who would love the history, and Pedro and Fernanda, for whom everything after Kyoto is new.
west-castles-inland-sea.suits: Carlos and Nadir (Hiroshima, Izumo Taisha, two original castle keeps), Pedro and Fernanda (four new bases after Kyoto), João and Carolina (Mt Misen and the climb inside Himeji's keep), Tatiana (plenty of variety without long days)
west-castles-inland-sea.trade: Almost no snow country: Matsue may get a dusting, but late December there is more often grey and wet than white. No Kanazawa, Takayama or Shirakawa-go, and Fuji only from the train window. The 28 Dec move from Hiroshima to Matsue is about four hours, the longest day of the trip, and a few of Matsue's sights have not yet published their New Year hours.
west-castles-inland-sea.nye: At a lakeside onsen hotel in Matsue: a kaiseki dinner with Lake Shinji's winter catch (shijimi clams, sea bass baked in paper), toshikoshi soba before midnight, a private or in-room bath, and osechi on New Year's morning. Matsue Red Cross Hospital, whose perinatal unit answers calls at night and over New Year, is about ten minutes away by taxi.

stay_notes.matsue: The New Year block. Four nights let the group sit still from 29 Dec to 1 Jan and spread Adachi, Izumo Taisha and the castle over three unhurried days, with the long arrival day followed by an easy one.
stay_notes.okayama: Arrive on the quiet 1 Jan and stay put through the busy 2–4 Jan, with short hops to Okayama (17 min) and Himeji (about an hour).
stay_notes.tokyo:2: Four nights for what was shut in December, a day trip, and a calm last day before the flight.

winter-food-trail.theme: Crab, Kobe beef, Hakata ramen and Nagoya eel
winter-food-trail.tagline: Seven bases over 20 nights (Tokyo 3, Kanazawa 3, Osaka 3, Arima Onsen 3, Fukuoka 4, Nagoya 2, Tokyo 2), eating each region's best in its winter season, with a ryokan feast for New Year.
winter-food-trail.feel: It opens in Tokyo's markets and department-store food halls, then rides the Hokuriku shinkansen to Kanazawa at the height of the crab season, with Omicho market lunches and oden at night. Osaka is three days of kushikatsu, takoyaki and a Kuromon morning, with a day in Kyoto's Nishiki market before the year-end crush. New Year is the calm in the middle: three nights at a ryokan in Arima, the old spa town in the hills above Kobe, with Kobe beef kaiseki and osechi on New Year's morning. On the quiet first of January you ride to Hakata for mizutaki, tonkotsu ramen and the yatai stalls as they reopen, then come back east through Nagoya for eel and miso before a last sushi dinner in Tokyo.
activities: Tokyo: Tsukiji outer market breakfast, Ginza and Nihonbashi food halls, Kappabashi kitchen street, monjayaki in Tsukishima, a yakitori alley
Kanazawa: Omicho market crab (female kobako crab only until the end of December), Kaga cooking such as jibuni duck stew, oden, a sake brewery, a wagashi sweets class
Osaka: Dotonbori and Shinsekai street food, Kuromon market at 9:00 before the crowds, fugu hot pot, a day in Kyoto for Nishiki market and the Fushimi sake district
Arima Onsen: Kobe beef kaiseki at the ryokan, carbonated-spring rice crackers, a day down in Kobe for a teppanyaki lunch and Nankinmachi's Chinatown
Fukuoka: Hakata ramen, mizutaki chicken hot pot, motsunabe, the yatai stalls as they reopen, Yanagawa's steamed eel and kotatsu boats
Nagoya: hitsumabushi grilled eel, miso-katsu, tebasaki wings, miso-nikomi udon, Atsuta Shrine and the castle

For Fernanda at every stop: cooked crab, hot pots, tempura, grilled fish, well-done Kobe beef and grilled (not raw) mentaiko are all fine. Skip raw oysters and shellfish, crab sashimi, raw chicken (torisashi, common in Kyushu), horse sashimi and the raw egg with sukiyaki; keep tuna and kinmedai to a small portion a week; sushi only at a good counter. Ryokan will cook the sashimi course if told when booking
winter-food-trail.why: For a family that plans its days around lunch. It follows the calendar closely: city eating before 29 Dec and after 2 Jan, and a ryokan with every meal included while the restaurants close.
winter-food-trail.suits: João and Carolina (the most new food), Pedro (who knows Tokyo and Kyoto but not Hakata, Arima or Nagoya), Carlos and Nadir (markets and the ryokan New Year), Tatiana. Fernanda has the most to skip at raw counters, so each base has cooked classics picked out for her.
winter-food-trail.trade: Seven bases and six moves make it the busiest of these routes, with two long days (Hakata on 1 Jan, Nagoya on 5 Jan) and little rest between. Almost no snow, no close Fuji view, no Takayama, and Kyoto only as a day. Yamanashi's hoto belongs to the Fuji route instead, because there is no sensible way to fit Yamanashi in after Hakata. Food spending is high: crab and Kobe beef dinners run ¥15–50k a head.
winter-food-trail.nye: At a ryokan in Arima Onsen: a kaiseki dinner built around Kobe beef (cooked through for Fernanda) and winter crab, toshikoshi soba before midnight, a private bath, and osechi with Kansai-style white-miso ozoni on 1 Jan. The two public baths shut on 1 Jan, but the ryokan baths do not. Kobe's large hospitals are 25–35 minutes away by taxi.

stay_notes.kanazawa: Two full days and an arrival afternoon for Omicho, a crab dinner, Kenroku-en and a sweets class, all before the market closes for New Year.
stay_notes.osaka: Three nights, one of them spent on a Kyoto day, so Osaka itself gets two food days without hurrying.
stay_notes.arima: The New Year block, fixed by the calendar: a one-hour hop on 29 Dec, three nights with every meal included while restaurants shut, and a day down in Kobe on 30 Dec.
stay_notes.fukuoka: Arrive on the quiet 1 Jan and stay through 2–4 Jan while the stalls and restaurants reopen; the first full day is an easy one.
stay_notes.nagoya: A stopping place that halves the return from Hakata, and a food city in its own right: one full day for eel, miso and the castle.

fuji-pacific-shore.theme: Sunny winter days around Fuji and the sea
fuji-pacific-shore.tagline: Six bases over 20 nights (Tokyo 2, Kawaguchiko 3, Atami 3, Shuzenji 4, Ise-Shima 4, Tokyo 4), staying on the dry, bright Pacific side with Fuji in its clearest month.
fuji-pacific-shore.feel: Two days in Tokyo, then straight to Lake Kawaguchi for three dawns with Fuji across the water, hoto stew and a lakeside Christmas. On 25 Dec you drop down to Atami on the coast in time for the winter fireworks over the bay, and spend two mild days on the Izu shore, with capybaras soaking in yuzu baths and the sea cliffs at Jogasaki. The four nights over New Year are in Shuzenji, a quiet onsen town of bamboo and river, with strawberry farms in season, Fuji across Suruga Bay from a ropeway and a major perinatal hospital fifteen minutes away. On New Year's Day you ride west to Ise-Shima for spiny lobster, pearl divers and Japan's most sacred shrine at dawn, then finish with four days in Tokyo and a calm day in Kamakura.
activities: Tokyo: Tsukiji and Hama-rikyu, Fuji from a tower at sunset, Asakusa
Kawaguchiko: the Panoramic Ropeway at opening time, Oishi Park on the north shore, Oshino Hakkai's spring ponds, the Itchiku Kubota kimono museum, hoto for dinner
Atami: the bay fireworks on 25 Dec, the MOA Museum of Art, the Kiunkaku villa, the capybaras' yuzu bath at Izu Shaboten Zoo, Jogasaki's suspension bridge for the fit four
Shuzenji: the temple and the bamboo path, foot baths, strawberry picking in Izu-Nagaoka, Fuji across Suruga Bay from the Izu Panorama Park ropeway, the Mishima Skywalk
Ise-Shima: Mikimoto Pearl Island and the ama divers, Toba Aquarium, Ago Bay from the Yokoyama lookout, Ise Jingu at dawn, akafuku sweets in Okage Yokocho, spiny lobster
Tokyo and Kamakura: the Great Buddha and Hase-dera on a quiet weekday, Tokyo National Museum, a single act at Kabuki-za
fuji-pacific-shore.why: The warm-weather route, built for comfort: the sunniest stretch of Japan in winter, very little ice, short moves until New Year, and an onsen ryokan with a large hospital nearby. It suits anyone who wants Fuji at its best and the sea rather than snow.
fuji-pacific-shore.suits: Fernanda most of all (flat towns, mild days, private baths, short moves), Carlos and Nadir (Fuji dawns, Ise Jingu, a ryokan New Year), Tatiana; João and Carolina get the Fuji dawns, Chureito's steps and Jogasaki's cliffs, though less to push themselves on.
fuji-pacific-shore.trade: No snow, no Kanazawa or Kyoto, and fewer museums and big-city days than the main route. Two moves of about four hours (1 and 5 Jan) to reach Ise-Shima and come back, and Ise Jingu is still busy on 4 Jan. Four ryokan nights over New Year make Shuzenji the dearest stay of any route here.
fuji-pacific-shore.nye: At a ryokan in Shuzenji: a kaiseki of Izu's winter fish (kinmedai simmered rather than raw, and a small portion for Fernanda because it is a high-mercury fish), toshikoshi soba, a private bath, and perhaps the temple bell at Shuzenji at midnight. Juntendo University Shizuoka Hospital, a comprehensive perinatal centre, is about fifteen minutes away in Izu-Nagaoka.

stay_notes.tokyo: Arrival and one full day; Tokyo's main share comes at the end, when museums have reopened.
stay_notes.kawaguchiko: Three dawns give three chances at a clear Fuji, and two full days fill the lake's sights without hurry.

stay_notes.ise-shima: Arrive on the quiet 1 Jan and wait out the busy 2–4 Jan by the sea; Ise Jingu goes on 4 Jan at dawn, when the crowds are thinner than on 1–3 Jan.
stay_notes.tokyo:2: Four nights for Tokyo's museums, Kamakura and an easy last day by the airport.

tohoku-snow-samurai.theme: Tohoku by shinkansen: snow, samurai and onsen
tohoku-snow-samurai.tagline: Six bases over 20 nights (Tokyo 3, Sendai 3, Morioka 4, Tsunagi Onsen 2, Aomori 4, Tokyo 4), riding the Tohoku shinkansen north into deep snow, with every move but the ride home under two and a half hours.
tohoku-snow-samurai.feel: After three days in Tokyo the Hayabusa takes ninety minutes to Sendai, where the zelkova avenue may still be lit for the Pageant of Starlight and Matsushima's pine islands are a seated cruise away. Morioka, a small, easy city of wanko soba and red-brick banks, is home for four nights, with day trips to the black-walled samurai lanes of Kakunodate and the golden hall of Chuson-ji, both under snow. New Year is two nights at an onsen hotel on Lake Gosho, with Mt Iwate white across the water. On the quiet first of January it is an hour north to Aomori, the snowiest city in Japan: Hirosaki Castle's park in deep snow, Nara Yoshitomo's great white dog at the art museum, and the Hakkoda ropeway among the forming snow monsters. Then one train carries you home.
activities: Tokyo: Tsukiji outer market and Hama-rikyu, Meiji Jingu and the Nezu Museum, Asakusa
Sendai: the Pageant of Starlight if it is still lit, grilled beef tongue, the Matsushima bay cruise and Zuigan-ji, Yamadera's 1,000 icy steps for the fit four only
Morioka: wanko soba, the castle-ruin park and the old brick bank, a day in Kakunodate's samurai district (Aoyagi house), a day at Chuson-ji's golden hall in Hiraizumi
Tsunagi Onsen: a lakeside onsen hotel with in-room baths, Mt Iwate over Lake Gosho, a slow New Year's Eve
Aomori: the Aomori Museum of Art and the Sannai-Maruyama Jomon site, the Nebuta float museum, Hirosaki Castle park in snow and its apple-pie cafés, the Hakkoda ropeway
Tokyo again: the firemen's parade on 6 Jan, Tokyo National Museum, Kabuki-za, a calm last day
tohoku-snow-samurai.why: The bold one: real snow through the middle fortnight without a single bus-dependent base or mountain road, because the shinkansen does all the work. It is also the cheapest route here by a clear margin. Best for anyone who wanted the Japan of snow-laden samurai houses and onsen steam.
tohoku-snow-samurai.suits: João and Carolina (snow, Hakkoda, Yamadera's steps), Carlos and Nadir (samurai towns, Chuson-ji, onsen), Tatiana, and Pedro and Fernanda, for whom all of it is new. Fernanda will want ice cleats and taxis, and should treat Kakunodate and Chuson-ji as slow days.
tohoku-snow-samurai.trade: Cold (often –5 °C) and icy underfoot, which is the main worry at 30 weeks. No Kyoto, Kanazawa or Fuji. Fewer museums are open over New Year, Morioka and Aomori are quiet towns rather than great cities, and the Hakkoda ropeway and day trips can be stopped by weather. The New Year base is the furthest from an obstetric unit of any route here.
tohoku-snow-samurai.nye: At an onsen hotel at Tsunagi on Lake Gosho, 25 minutes from Morioka: a winter kaiseki with Iwate beef and Sanriku fish, toshikoshi soba, a room with its own bath, and snow outside the window. The nearest obstetric centre, Iwate Medical University Hospital, is about 35–45 minutes away by taxi, so if that feels too far, spend all six nights in Morioka instead and book a New Year's Eve dinner at the hotel.

kii-coast-classic.theme: The classic cities, then New Year by the Pacific
kii-coast-classic.tagline: Tokyo 4, Kyoto 4, Shirahama 4, Nara 4 and Tokyo 4: four nights everywhere, only four moves, and New Year's Eve at a seaside onsen on the Kii peninsula.
kii-coast-classic.feel: Four nights in Tokyo for the first-timers, then Kyoto on Christmas Eve while every temple, castle and museum is open. On 28 Dec the Kuroshio express follows the coast south to Shirahama, one of Japan's oldest hot springs: white sand, a mild winter sea and a hotel with dinner included for New Year's Eve. One day goes inland to the Kumano shrines and the giant river bath dug at Kawayu each winter; others are for the fish market, the sea caves and sunset beside Engetsu island. On New Year's Day a quiet train takes you to Nara, where a whole house with its own bath is a short walk from Todai-ji and the deer. Mornings there are calm and the evenings are at home. Four easy days in Tokyo close it.
activities: Tokyo (start): Tsukiji outer market, Asakusa and Senso-ji, Meiji Jingu and Harajuku, the Christmas lights
Kyoto: Nijo Castle, Kiyomizu-dera and Higashiyama, Kyoto National Museum, Arashiyama, Kinkaku-ji, Fushimi Inari, an evening in Osaka
Shirahama: Sakinoyu seaside bath, Engetsu island at sunset, Sandanbeki cave and Senjojiki rocks, Toretore fish market
From Shirahama: Kumano Hongu Taisha, the great torii at Oyunohara and the Sennin-buro river bath at Kawayu (a day by hired van)
Nara: Todai-ji and the deer before 9:00, Kasuga Taisha, Nara National Museum (2–3 Jan), Naramachi lanes
From Nara: Horyu-ji, the world's oldest wooden temple buildings (open every day), and Uji's Byodo-in
Tokyo (end): Tokyo National Museum, Kabuki-za, a Fuji or Kamakura day, last shopping
kii-coast-classic.why: It keeps the classic Tokyo and Kyoto for the four first-timers, done before the shutdown, and gives Pedro and Fernanda three things they have not seen: the Kii coast, Kumano and Nara as a place to live rather than an afternoon. The Pacific side is the mildest and driest place to spend New Year, and four nights per base keeps the rhythm calm.
kii-coast-classic.suits: Pedro and Fernanda, for new ground and a seaside New Year; Carlos and Nadir, for Kumano and Horyu-ji; João, Carolina and Tatiana, for Tokyo and Kyoto at full strength and a day of shrines and river baths in the mountains.
kii-coast-classic.trade: No snow and no Fuji stay (Fuji is seen from the train, or on a day trip at the end). Shirahama is a small resort, not a famous old onsen street, and its hospital is a 20–25 minute drive. Kumano needs a long day in a van. Eight of the twenty nights are in Tokyo.
kii-coast-classic.nye: At an onsen hotel in Shirahama with New Year's Eve dinner and toshikoshi soba included, a short private soak and an early night, or a late walk on the beach. The coast is the mildest place in mainland Japan to spend New Year, and New Year's Day breakfast is osechi at the hotel before an easy train on the quietest travel day of the year.

stay_notes.tokyo: Arrival plus three full days in lights week; Tokyo returns at the end for the reopened museums.
stay_notes.kyoto: Arrive on Christmas Eve and get three full days while everything is open, including Nijo Castle's palace (closed 29–31 Dec) and the National Museum (closed 29 Dec – 1 Jan).
stay_notes.shirahama: Four nights wrap the peak days 29–31 Dec so nobody travels on them: one day for Kumano, one for the coast and the market, and an easy New Year's Eve.
stay_notes.nara: 1–5 Jan in Nara lets you reach Todai-ji and the deer before the day-trippers on 2–3 Jan, and sit out the return peak with Horyu-ji and Uji as short hops.
stay_notes.tokyo:2: Three full days once Tokyo has reopened, with a Fuji or Kamakura day, and a calm last night near the airport.
